deep.reconstruction:
Context. This is the hodograph part of Riemann's work on plane air waves of finite amplitude (1860). The Riemann invariants p, q are the independent variables. A potential w(p,q) is defined by (4) x-(u+a)t = w_p and (5) x-(u-a)t = w_q. On the previous page he notes that w_p and w_q satisfy the same linear equation §2(1) as w; differentiating gives this only if the coefficients are constant. He then substitutes them into the §2 representation formulas (§2 (5),(6)) for w_{p',q'}. In those formulas he replaces (w_p - w_pq) by w_q and (w_q + w_pq) by w_p.

Reading of §2(1) (my inference). These replacements mean the equation is w_pq = w_p - w_q, possibly after normalising a constant m to 1. This fits the Boyle–Mariotte (isothermal) case, where a is constant and logarithmic invariants give constant coefficients. The adjoint equation is v_pq + v_p - v_q = 0. On that reading the Riemann function, normalised to v(p',q')=1, must satisfy v_p = v on q=q' and v_q = -v on p=p'. My computation gives v = exp((p-p')-(q-q'))·J0(2·sqrt((p-p')(q-q'))). This is not on the page.

Formulas on the page:
(6) w_p(p',q') = (w_p v)|_C + ∫_B^C [ w_p (v - v_p) dp + w_q v dq ]
(7) w_q(p',q') = (w_q v)|_B + ∫_B^C [ w_p v dp + w_q (v + v_q) dq ]
Here B is the point of the initial line t=0 where q=q', and C the point where p=p'. Riemann's ∫_{q'}^{p'} is shorthand for integrating along t=0 from x_B to x_C.

Initial data. At t=0, (4) and (5) give w_p = x and w_q = x. So one substitutes p(x,0), q(x,0) and w_p = w_q = x, and integrates in x from x_B to x_C.

Derivation (my filling-in). Let ω1 = w_p(v-v_p)dp + w_q v dq and ω2 = w_p v dp + w_q(v+v_q)dq.
- Exactness of ω1: ∂_q[w_p(v-v_p)] - ∂_p[w_q v] = -w_p(v_pq + v_p - v_q), using w_pq = w_p - w_q. This vanishes by the adjoint equation.
- Exactness of ω2: ∂_q[w_p v] - ∂_p[w_q(v+v_q)] = w_q(v_pq + v_p - v_q) = 0 likewise.
- Integrate around the characteristic triangle A=(p',q'), B, C.
- For ω1: on AB (q=q') the integrand v - v_p is 0. On CA (p=p') we have (w_p v)_q = -w_q v. Hence ∫_C^A ω1 = (w_p v)_C - w_p(A), which yields (6), evaluated at C.
- For ω2: on CA the factor v + v_q is 0. On AB we have (w_q v)_p = w_p v. This yields (7), evaluated at B.

Second part: the non-univalent case. Riemann extends validity to the case where p, q repeat values or are constant on stretches between the initial positions of p' and q', so that w is no longer a single-valued function of (p,q).
- Work in the (x,t)-plane. Take the region swept, from t=0 until the two values p' and q' meet, by the x-interval between them; this is the characteristic triangle in (x,t).
- The integrands, pulled back via p(x,t), q(x,t), w_p = x-(u+a)t and w_q = x-(u-a)t, stay single-valued there.
- Their integrals around the boundary of this region vanish. The justification is Green's theorem: ∮(P dp + Q dq) = 0 if P (in q) and Q (in p) vary continuously and ∂P/∂q = ∂Q/∂p. This is proved by integrating ∬(∂P/∂q - ∂Q/∂p) dp dq over the region.
- The vanishing of these two boundary integrals (relabelled '(7)' in the margin) then gives the formulas (6) exactly as in §2.
errors: The claim on the previous page that w_p, w_q satisfy the same equation as w by mere differentiation holds only if the coefficients of §2(1) are constant. That is consistent with the page's substitutions (w_pq = w_p - w_q) but not with the general variable-coefficient Riemann equation.

The boundary term in (6) carries subscript p',q' (partly overwritten). Strictly it must be evaluated at the initial point C where p=p' (subscript p'), just as (7) correctly has subscript q'. This is a notational slip or ambiguity.

Green's-theorem sufficiency condition is stated loosely ('P mit q und Q mit p stetig'). Also the claim that the argument carries over to the (x,t)-region when (x,t)->(p,q) is not injective is asserted as 'leicht' without detail. It is correct in substance, since the pull-back of a closed form is closed.

Equation numbering is in flux: both formulas are labelled (6)/(7) and a marginal (7) is attached to the vanishing integrals. The final sentence 'Aus den beiden Gleichungen (7) ... die Gleichungen (6)' uses the new numbering.

results.what: Representation of w_p, w_q at (p',q') by boundary values of v times data plus line integrals along the initial line t=0 (formulas 6,7), with initial data w_p = w_q = x
results.modern_name: Riemann's method / Riemann function for the linear hyperbolic (hodograph) equation; solution of the Cauchy problem for the gas-dynamics equations via the hodograph transform
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann 1860 (Über die Fortpflanzung ebener Luftwellen von endlicher Schwingungsweite)

results.what: Extension to the case where w is multivalued in (p,q), by working in the (x,t) domain of dependence and using vanishing of closed-form integrals
results.modern_name: Domain-of-dependence argument; pull-back of closed forms / Green's theorem on the characteristic triangle

results.what: Sufficient condition for vanishing of ∮(P dp + Q dq): continuity and ∂P/∂q = ∂Q/∂p, proved via the double integral
results.modern_name: Green's theorem / exactness of closed forms
